problem: Consider the equation $\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x+\frac{\pi }{3})=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}$ for $-\pi <x\le \pi .$ If the exact solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3}$ and ${x}_{4}$ are written in ascending order, what is the value of ${x}_{2}+{x}_{3}?$

feedback.problem: Consider the equation $\sqrt{3}\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x+\frac{\pi }{6})+3=0$ for $-\pi <x\le \pi .$ If the exact solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3}$ and ${x}_{4}$ are written in ascending order, what is the value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{4}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{3}\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x+\frac{\pi }{6})+3 & =0 \\ \sqrt{3}\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x+\frac{\pi }{6}) & =-3 \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡(2x+\frac{\pi }{6}) & =-\frac{3}{\sqrt{3}} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡(2x+\frac{\pi }{6}) & =-\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+\frac{\pi }{6} & =-\frac{\pi }{3}+n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the equation above for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & =-\frac{\pi }{3}-\frac{\pi }{6}+n\pi  \\ 2x & =-\frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi  \\ x & =-\frac{\pi }{4}+\frac{n\pi }{2} \\ x & =\frac{(2n-1)\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain $-\pi <x\le \pi .$

- Setting $n=-1$ gives $x=-\frac{3\pi }{4}$

- Setting $n=0$ gives $x=-\frac{\pi }{4}$

- Setting $n=1$ gives $x=\frac{\pi }{4}$

- Setting $n=2$ gives $x=\frac{3\pi }{4}$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain $-\pi <x\le \pi .$ So, the solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3},{x}_{4}$ (written in ascending order) are

$$
x=-\frac{3\pi }{4},\,-\frac{\pi }{4},\,\frac{\pi }{4},\,\frac{3\pi }{4}
$$

Finally, since ${x}_{1}=-\frac{3\pi }{4}$ and ${x}_{4}=\frac{3\pi }{4},$ we have

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{4}=-\frac{3\pi }{4}+\frac{3\pi }{4}=0.
$$
